 Time: 3:30 p.m. ET
 TV: Peacock
 Analyst: Zak Hanshew
 Combo: 4.44x 
 Payton Pritchard Over 14.5 points
 Over 221.5 total points
 Celtics moneyline
 Boston enters this matchup on a four-game winning streak and has averaged 128 points over its last three contests. The Magic will be without Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs, creating an appealing matchup for Payton Pritchard. He's averaging 16.6 points per game and faces an Orlando defense that has allowed 121.5 points per game over its last two outings.
 Zak Hanshew expects a high-scoring game and is pairing Pritchard's scoring total with the Over 221.5 and a Celtics moneyline victory. Read the full Celtics vs. Magic prediction and picks for the complete breakdown.
 Nets vs. Pacers
 Time: 5 p.m. ET
 TV: League Pass and YES Network
 Analyst: Shawn Krest
 Combo: 13.00x 
 Pacers -3.5
 Over 230.5 total points
 First-half Under 117.5
 Indiana is looking to snap a three-game losing streak against a Brooklyn team still searching for its first win. Both teams have struggled defensively and play at a fast pace, setting up a favorable spot for the full-game Over 230.5.
 The first-half Under 117.5 offers a different angle. Indiana averages 56 first-half points, while Brooklyn averages 53, making a lower-scoring opening half an appealing addition to this three-leg combination. Krest is also backing the Pacers to cover against a Nets team missing Egor Demin and Mikel Brown Jr.
 Read the full Nets vs. Pacers prediction and picks for the complete breakdown.
 Clippers vs. Warriors
 Time: 8:30 p.m. ET
 TV: ClipperVision, NBCS-Bay Area
 Analyst: Tom Oldfield
 Combo: 5.75x 
 Clippers +2.5
 Under 221.5 points
 Yaxel Lendeborg Over 7.5 rebounds
 Golden State has won three straight games, but the Warriors will be without Stephen Curry and Draymond Green for this matchup. Tom Oldfield sees an opportunity for the Clippers to keep this one close, especially with Darius Garland leading the offense against a Golden State defense that ranks in the bottom third of the NBA in defensive rating.
 The Under 221.5 also makes sense with the Clippers averaging just 105.4 points per game, the second-lowest mark in the league. The Under has cashed in two of their last three games, while Yaxel Lendeborg has grabbed at least nine rebounds in four of his last five outings. With Green out, Oldfield expects the rookie's rebounding production to climb.
 Read the full Clippers vs. Warriors predictions for the complete breakdown.
 Raptors vs. Lakers
 Time: 9 p.m. ET
 TV: Spectrum Sports Network, Sportsnet
 Analyst: Chris Walder
 Combo: 9.86x 
 Raptors moneyline
 Under 227.5 points
 RJ Barrett Over 20.5 points
 Toronto has a chance to end its seven-game losing streak against the Lakers, and Chris Walder is backing the Raptors to pull off the road upset. The key will be slowing down Luka Doncic and limiting his ability to dictate the offense. Toronto is looking to rebound defensively after allowing 121 points to Orlando on Friday.
 RJ Barrett is a strong candidate to lead the way offensively. He's averaged 25.5 points per game across four meetings with the Lakers as a Raptor and has cleared Sunday's 20.5-point line in three of those contests. The Under 227.5 rounds out the combo, with both teams combining for a 5-6 record in the total market.
 Read the full Raptors vs. Lakers predictions for the complete breakdown.
